findings: Current OSS search accepts query, top_k and filters; identity kwargs at the top level are rejected.
At least one entity filter is required upstream; Gravitre requires its full tenant/subject/agent scope.
Memory construction initializes embedder, vector store, LLM and history storage. Do not instantiate defaults during research.
add defaults infer to true; automatic extraction/update/delete is not authorized by this benchmark.
delete accepts an ID without tenant arguments; any future adapter must verify ownership before invoking it.
Telemetry, model/vector dependencies, retention semantics and deletion readback still require an isolated SDK assessment.
The current repository redirects active work to letta-code and calls the archive branch's V1 API server retired.
Current source is an agent harness with MemFS, self-editing memory/skills/prompts and cross-agent search. These behaviors are not adopted.
Memory tree validation has trusted configuration for read-only files, depth and character limits; it is not Gravitre tenant/subject consent enforcement.
Use only a future read-only scoped snapshot boundary for comparison; no old API endpoint is assumed and no second orchestrator is introduced.
Source review is architectural evidence, not a measured retrieval, deletion, latency or naturalness benchmark.
